Subject: Amara's small pottery room above a shop BEFORE eviction. Her simple working pottery wheel stands close to a narrow window, clay basin and a damp board within reach, six narrow blue-banded clay jugs waiting on a shelf above folded bedding, room for people to pass only by turning sideways. A handworked cup and a spare handle on the wooden board. Worn plaster carries clay smudges. Beautiful but modest carved timber window screen, patterned old tiled sill, glimpses of layered Cartharan arches and roof gardens through the window. Warm daylight illuminates honest ongoing work. No person or identifiable portrait is needed. Do not turn this poor family's room into a palace or commercial factory. Compose a landscape 3:2 intimate architectural interior plate, wheel and blue-banded jugs clearly readable.
assets.conversion: Sharp WebP quality 88, effort 6; format conversion only, no resizing, cropping, recoloring, compositing, or retouching.
assets.inspection: Visual check: wheel close to window, six blue-banded jugs above folded bedding, cup and spare handle, small worn workroom.

Subject: an imposing Cartharan petition court beneath a deep ornate arcade, cool shade and a narrow blade of daylight on worn paving. A modest queue of ordinary petitioners holding folded papers waits before a seated clerk at a wooden writing desk. This is a fictional Mediterranean/Middle Eastern civic bureaucracy, not a modern courthouse: no courtroom benches, gavels, modern uniforms or flags. Subject: intimate still life of EXACTLY FIVE hand-formed clay bowls on a worn wooden pottery bench, separate clearly countable silhouettes, slightly uneven rims and a subtle thumbprint visible in the nearest bowl. These are ordinary earthenware bowls at different modest stages of drying, not jeweled or gilded treasures. A folded work cloth beside them; a softly indicated carved courtyard screen and sliver of old tile behind the bench, warm courtyard sunlight grazing clay texture. No people, no corpse, no grief symbolism, no extra pots or bowls anywhere. Let the illustration emphasize capable patient handwork and the value of useful things. Square composition, fine ink detail concentrated on the bowls and wood, architecture only lightly suggested; generous irregular ivory paper edges. Vignette suitable between passages of a novel.

Subject: a healer's lived-in worktable viewed from a high oblique angle. An open handmade stitched notebook with thick uneven paper is the focus, containing only faint abstract pen strokes and loose page divisions, absolutely no legible text, numbers, formulae, recipes or instructions. Nearby a few modest glazed ceramic vessels, small brass balance weights, a folded cloth and a simple pen. Fine carved woodwork and the shadow of an intricate mashrabiya screen quietly establish the Mediterranean/Middle Eastern setting. Filtered morning light, evidence of careful repeated observation and useful teaching, not magical spectacle. No recognizable drug substances, no syringes, no modern lab equipment, no flames. Landscape 3:2 close still life, richly hand-drawn textures and softly fading warm ivory paper edges.
